author: Income Machine
title: An Interview With 'The Bear'
text:
Well, that happened fast.
It seems like just yesterweek indexes were trading at all-time highs, and confidence in the global economy and stock markets was ebullient. Okay, it was actually since October. But ever since, the market endured a sharp descent like a runway skier fresh off a chairlift in the Rockies. The NASDAQ ( QQQ ) Composite closed down more than 20% from its all-time high, waking the bear from its typical slumber during the annual Santa Rally.
It was difficult to lock down the Bear for an interview since he was booked pretty solid with televised appearances, but I was able to secure a few minutes to sit down and pick his brain about his sudden and unexpected arrival. Below is the transcript from our discussion:
Source: Image
Me: Thanks for joining us today, Bear. We weren't expecting you so soon. Many economists forecasted your arrival late next year or early 2020. What gives?
Bear: Me and Rodney Dangerfield. We can't get no respect. Even a 10-year absence doesn't make the heart grow fonder, eh? I made such a splash in 2008 that people tremble at even the thought of me. You think I want to be here? I'm supposed to be hibernating...
Me: As a long-term investor, I am happy you're here. The Bull was getting long in the tooth. I have been biding my time waiting for an opportune time to buy stocks, but everything has been way too pricey. What is your plan now that you're here? Do you intend to stick around for a while?
Bear: I'll say. Bull, bull, bull, that's all I've been hearing on my Spotify podcasts month after month in my cave. And heck, Spotify didn’t even exist when I took my latest sabbatical. What a bunch of bull. Let me show you something.
(Bear pauses and pulls out a 10-year chart of the NASDAQ depicted below)
Source: Charles Schwab
Bear (continued): What about this looks sustainable to you? People buying the NASDAQ above 8k? Are these the same folks buying oceanfront property in Phoenix? They only have themselves to blame. The answer is yes, I intend to stick around for 6-12 months.
Me: That should give us plenty of time to buy. But my real question is why are you here? Why now ?
Bear: Why now? Why not now!? Look let me show you something else.
(Bear pulls out another chart. This time of the Shiller PE Ratio)
Source: Shiller PE Ratio
Bear (continued): Look, I'm providing a public service. I'm saving folks from themselves. I wouldn't have such a bad reputation if folks could just dial back some of their greed and stop pouring money into an already overheated market. Let me provide some of the reasons I'm here:
1) The era of cheap money via accommodative monetary policy is coming to a close. And it's long overdue. Let me tell you something, TINA worked for a long time, but TINA has aged, and quite frankly, she ain't as cute as she used to be. The Fed has been slow to move, but they're doing the right thing normalizing policy.
Me: Let me stop you there. I agree. There's a lot of political animosity directed toward the Fed, but people forget that interest rates remain historically low. It's my turn to share a chart. Take a look at this:
Source: MacroTrends
Bear: (nodding). That’s reason number one. The second reason I'm here is due to all this protectionism nonsense. Trade wars aren't conducive for strategic planning for corporations. Take the U.K as an example. There's so much ambiguity with regards to Brexit that corporations are fleeing by the day . The same concerns apply domestically in the United States. Think about companies trading on the NASDAQ: Facebook ( FB ), Netflix ( NFLX ), Apple ( AAPL ), and Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ). These guys have tremendous international exposure; what they gain in one place can be lost in another in the event of a trade war. But this is a temporary setback. Once globalism is out of the bag, it's hard to bottle it back in. It's kind of like this present I sent to my ol' pal Bull for Christmas. Happy Holidays old friend!
Source: Image
Me: I'm sure he's thrilled. Any other reasons?
Bear: Some folks have alleged tax-loss harvesting and a mixed Congress come January, but neither of those have any teeth. No canines at least - tertiary reasons at best. Then, there's depressed oil prices, but that's actually a boon for most sectors as we saw from 2014 to 2018. The main reason I am here is simply to let some air out of the ballooned market and restore a little sanity. Technically, I won't overstay my welcome. Speaking of technically, let me show you some key technical levels where stocks will likely bottom out:
Source: Charles Schwab
Bear (continued): Same thing applies to the S&P 500.
Source: Charles Schwab
Bear (continued): You see, I'm like the Fed. I'm practically telegraphing my moves.
Me: Well thanks for that. So, no reason for 2008-level panic? We're not gonna see a full-fledged market meltdown coupled with a painful recession?
Bear: Fat chance. Or is it slim chance? I never did figure that one out. No. I'm no Silicon Valley techie here to disrupt the peace. Just a quick slap to the face and then it's back to bed for a few years. The economy remains strong and cooler heads will prevail regarding tariffs. The Fed is very attuned and moderate, and profits will continue to roll in. No reason for pandemonium.
Me: That's a relief. Do you ever wonder why so many investors dislike you?
Bear: Isn't it obvious? Michael Jordan was a bull. The bears had Jay Cutler and Rex Grossman. Even I can't blame 'em.
Me: Well, thanks again for your time.
That was our chat and the bear shuffled off to his next appointment. This market pullback that manifested into a bear market is long overdue, and investors should embrace this opportunity to find the gems battered down within the indiscriminate selling. I am in no rush, but I am excited to be back to being an active buyer again. As the bear said, this is most likely a benign and generic pullback and not the second coming of the Great Recession.
In my estimation, the bottom is within 5-10% from here. It's almost time to pounce and join the bear in his holiday revelries.
Disclosure: I am/we are long APPL, NFLX, QQQ. I wrote this article myself, and it expresses my own opinions. I am not receiving compensation for it (other than from Seeking Alpha). I have no business relationship with any company whose stock is mentioned in this article.
